clue.text: Point to stroke in bad calligraphy

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
the crawl is a swimming stroke

explanation.surface: Someone points at a pen stroke in a page of poor handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is untidy, hurried handwriting, the opposite of fine penmanship.

clue.text: Backs up in athletic contests

indicators.note: the word up is placed inside the word for athletic contests

parts.note: sports are athletic contests
taken as written

explanation.surface: A coach describes reserve players stepping in during an athletics meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backs up' reads as one phrasal verb, but the definition is 'Backs' alone and 'up' goes inside SPORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To back someone is to give them support, a verb used in the third person.

clue.text: School near resort is without a dictionary

indicators.note: is without here means stands outside, so the rearranged word is wrapped round the dictionary
read as re-sort, sort again, telling us to rearrange the letters of near

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A school by the seaside apparently has no dictionary in its library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town (fitting, since the school stands on the Sussex coast near Brighton) but read as 're-sort' it rearranges NEAR into REAN, which goes round OED.
explanation.definitionFit: Roedean is a well-known girls' boarding school on the English south coast.

clue.text: Naturalist goes to club about one, for fish

parts.note: Gilbert White was the famous eighteenth-century naturalist of Selborne

indicators.note: the club word stands about, surrounding, the letter for one

parts.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A nature lover heads to their club to talk about fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert White wrote The Natural History of Selborne, a classic of English nature writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitebait are the tiny young of herring and sprat, eaten fried whole.

clue.text: Alienate by replacement of Grant in see perhaps

indicators.note: replacement means the letters are put back in new places, so they are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bishop's diocese seems to have turned against a man called Grant who was moved there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a bishop's diocese, with Grant sent in to replace someone; in fact both words are anagram fodder, and 'in' and 'perhaps' only join them.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange people is to make them hostile or distant from one another.

clue.text: Do they end in workers having a rise?

definitions.text: Do they end in workers having a rise?

parts.words: Do they end in workers having a rise?
parts.note: a rise sounds like a pay increase, but it is also getting up on your feet; protests where workers stay seated finish when they stand up

explanation.surface: A question about whether industrial action wins pay increases.
explanation.walkthrough: The strike seems to end with a pay rise; the joke is that a protest by sitting down ends when the workers rise from their seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Protests in which workers occupy the workplace and refuse to work, staying seated where they are.

clue.text: Just the outfit to take the voltage

parts.note: a rig, or rig-out, is an outfit of clothes or equipment
HT is short for high tension, a high voltage

explanation.surface: An electrician has exactly the kit needed to handle the voltage.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and fair are synonyms: a just cause is a fair and proper one.

clue.text: 29's evacuee holds one Bible version in a Buddhist state

indicators.note: holds means the dog's name grips the other letters inside it

parts.note: 29 is the dog's home in Peter Pan; Nana, the Darlings' dog, is turned out of it when Mr Darling moves in
I is the Roman numeral for one
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone evacuated from a building carries a Bible into a Buddhist place of peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 across is the kennel. In J M Barrie's Peter Pan, Mr Darling lives in the dog Nana's kennel as penance, so Nana is the one turned out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism, nirvana is the final state of enlightenment, freed from desire and rebirth.

clue.text: Season in France without transport? What a game

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the French season wraps round the vehicle

parts.note: ete is French for summer
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in France for the summer with no car exclaims about a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking', but here it means 'outside', so ETE goes round CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecarte is a card game for two players using a short deck.

clue.text: Agile, trenchant characters can provide home comfort

indicators.note: characters here means the letters of the two words, which can be rebuilt into something else

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lively, sharp-witted people make a household pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' seems to mean people, but it means the letters of AGILE and TRENCHANT, which are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm house in winter is a basic domestic comfort provided by radiators and a boiler.

clue.text: I'd put in now to see the governor

indicators.note: put in means the letters of I'd are placed inside the word for now

parts.note: the present is now
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone decides to call on the state governor right away.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of a college, society or company, its chief officer.

clue.text: Italian lake retreat for a Doctor Silver

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the whole string of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A doctor called Silver takes a holiday by an Italian lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a holiday hideaway, but it reverses A, DR and AG, which read GA RD A backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Garda is the largest lake in Italy, in the north between Brescia and Verona.

clue.text: Lower the fare excessively

parts.note: lower seems to mean reduce a price, but read as putting food down the throat it means eating the meal too much

explanation.surface: A demand that ticket prices be cut too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' looks like a bus or train price and 'Lower' like cutting it; in fact the fare is food and to lower it is to swallow it.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat more than is good for you, gorging beyond what you need.

clue.text: Striking actors in Ishmael for example?

parts.note: workers who are out are on strike
the cast is the group of actors in a play

explanation.surface: Actors on strike appear in a play about Ishmael.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Ishmael is sent away with his mother Hagar into the wilderness, the type of the rejected exile; the question mark marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A person rejected and driven out by family or society, as Ishmael was.

clue.text: Taunton garage parts with native vehicle

indicators.note: parts means the answer comes from parts of the two words, running across them

explanation.surface: A garage in Taunton, a town in Somerset, sells off a local cart.
explanation.walkthrough: Taunton is the county town of Somerset in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonga is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage used in India.

clue.text: Jack takes lass to Leatherhead-that's unusual ()

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is a sailor too
Norma is a girl's name

indicators.note: head means the first letter, the front of the word leather

explanation.surface: A sailor takes his girlfriend to Leatherhead, a town in Surrey, which is out of character.
explanation.walkthrough: Leatherhead is a town in Surrey, but the clue splits it: 'head' of 'Leather' gives L. AB is the usual crossword sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abnormal departs from what is normal or typical, which is to say unusual.

clue.text: Scamp is in favour of splitting discount

indicators.note: splitting means the word for in favour of breaks the discount word apart and sits inside

parts.note: a rebate is a discount or partial refund
pro means in favour of

explanation.surface: A rascal backs a scheme to split a price reduction.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled rogue, a rascal beyond reform.

clue.text: Olga and I composed this line

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are arranged into a new word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people claim to have written a line of verse together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' and 'line' suggest poetry, but the line is a slanting one and 'composed' rearranges OLGA AND I.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagonal is a straight line joining opposite corners, running on a slant.

clue.text: Fancy going into a bar!

definitions.meaning: a whim or odd notion, an eccentric idea
a musical note of one beat, fitted with others into a bar of music

explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' and the exclamation mark suggest a pub visit; the bar is a measure of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Crotchet means both a quirky whim and a quarter note, several of which fill a bar.

clue.text: Goes for mending?

definitions.meaning: to go somewhere, as in betaking yourself to a place

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the formal 'repair to the drawing room', meaning go there.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair to a place is to go there, and repairs are acts of mending.

clue.text: Soprano gets pie in car

indicators.note: in ear means what is heard, so the word for a pie is taken by its sound

parts.note: a patty is a small pie or pasty

explanation.surface: A singer is handed a pie while listening.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'car', but the clue needs 'ear': heard, a patty is the opera singer's name. Adelina Patti was a celebrated nineteenth-century soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelina Patti was one of the most famous operatic sopranos of the Victorian era.

clue.text: Coachwork in some form, perhaps

parts.note: coachwork looks like a vehicle body, but it is the work of a coach, a teacher, given to a school class or form

explanation.surface: A garage offers bodywork in one style or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coachwork' suggests a car body and 'form' its shape; the coach is a tutor and the form a school class.
explanation.definitionFit: Teaching or instruction, especially paid private lessons given by a tutor.

clue.text: Notes point tax officer raised

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the pieces are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
VAT is value added tax
CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: A tax inspector draws up notes on a point he raised.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'raised', turns the whole run E VAT CO upwards, giving the eight-note span.
explanation.definitionFit: An octave is a span of eight notes of the scale, from one note to its double.

clue.text: Outdo girl star

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo or top it
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl outshines everyone as a star.
explanation.definitionFit: Capella is the brightest star in the constellation Auriga.

clue.text: Faithful ally troubled about nothing

indicators.note: about here means the rearranged letters go round the letter for nothing
troubled means stirred up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A loyal friend frets over nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges ALLY to LYAL, and 'about' wraps that round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyal and faithful are synonyms, describing steadfast allegiance.

clue.text: Housewife's work for some evening out?

definitions.meaning: pressing clothes with a hot iron, a household chore
evening here is making even, smoothing creases flat, not a night out

explanation.walkthrough: 'evening out' looks like a night on the town; it is making something even, and pressing is one way of doing that.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing is the domestic chore of pressing laundry, and ironing out means smoothing flat.

clue.text: Friendliness — the girl's full of it

indicators.note: full of means the girl's name is filled with the other word, wrapping round it

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name; the 's stands for is
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl full of herself shows a friendly nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is friendly relations, goodwill between people or nations.

clue.text: Repeating something to do with quarter share

parts.note: it can stand for a thing, an unspecified something
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass
a ration is a fixed share or allowance

explanation.surface: Someone keeps repeating a point about dividing things into quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to do with' only joins the definition to the wordplay; the compass quarters are N, E, S and W.
explanation.definitionFit: Iteration is the act of doing or saying something again, repetition.

clue.text: Poor Neil's got time for storing fodder

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the letters of Neil's are put into a different order

parts.note: the letters of Neil with the S of the 's included
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A struggling farmer called Neil has time to store hay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges NEILS into ENSIL, and AGE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensilage is the process of preserving green crops as silage for animal feed.

clue.text: Darling Daddy's penitentiary

parts.note: Darling looks like an endearment, but it is the family name in Peter Pan, whose father punishes himself by living in the dog's house

explanation.surface: A child's pet name for a father who is in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: In J M Barrie's Peter Pan, Mr Darling, ashamed of chaining up Nana the dog, lives in her outdoor shelter as penance until the children return.
explanation.definitionFit: A doghouse is a small outdoor shelter for a dog, where Mr Darling serves his self-imposed sentence.
